The '''US-China Business Council''' ('''USCBC''') is a [[501(c)(6) organization|501(c)(6)]] [[nonprofit organization]] whose stated goal is promoting trade between the [[United States]] and the [[China|People's Republic of China]] (PRC). As of 2024, it comprises over 270 American companies that trade and do business with the PRC.<ref>{{Cite web |title=About the US-China Business Council |url=https://www.uschina.org/about |access-date=September 10, 2024 |website=US-China Business Council}}</ref>

==History==
The council was founded in 1973 with the support of the [[White House]], the [[Department of State]] and the [[Department of Commerce]] as the National Council for United States-China Trade. [[Frederick B. Dent]], the then [[United States Secretary of Commerce]], compiled an executive committee for the council out of several prominent business leaders.<ref name="FL">{{cite web |title=UNITED STATES-CHINA BUSINESS COUNCIL Records, 1973‑78 (1983) |url=https://www.fordlibrarymuseum.gov/library/guides/findingaid/United%20States-China%20Business%20Council%20-%20Records.htm |website=Ford Library Museum |access-date=30 December 2018 |archive-date=7 May 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210507224204/https://www.fordlibrarymuseum.gov/library/guides/findingaid/united%20states-china%20business%20council%20-%20records.htm |url-status=live }}</ref>

The executive committee first met on March 22, 1973, to begin the formation of the council, with the executive committee members being the first Board of Directors. [[Donald C. Burnham]], of [[Westinghouse Corporation]], took the post of chairman and the Board elected [[Christopher H. Phillips]] to be the first president.<ref name="FL" /> Phillips would serve as president of the council until his retirement in 1986.<ref>{{cite web |title=Nomination of Christopher H. Phillips To Be United States Ambassador to Brunei |url=https://www.presidency.ucsb.edu/documents/nomination-christopher-h-phillips-be-united-states-ambassador-brunei |website=The American Presidency Project |access-date=30 December 2018 |archive-date=2 September 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190902181243/https://www.presidency.ucsb.edu/documents/nomination-christopher-h-phillips-be-united-states-ambassador-brunei |url-status=live }}</ref>

In the first year, the Council attracted 200 members and, by 1982, this had grown to 400 members.<ref name="FL" /> In 1974, the council began publishing the ''[[China Business Review]]'', a journal aimed at American companies trying to enter the Chinese market. In 1979, the Council opened an office in [[Beijing]].<ref>{{cite web |title=China Business Review |url=https://www.scimagojr.com/journalsearch.php?q=12253&tip=sid&clean=0 |website=Scimago Journal & Country Rank |access-date=8 January 2019 |archive-date=3 December 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211203112629/https://www.scimagojr.com/journalsearch.php?q=12253&tip=sid&clean=0 |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=USCBC Announces Relaunch of China Business Review |url=https://www.uschina.org/media/press/uscbc-announces-relaunch-china-business-review |website=The US-China Business Council |date=6 April 2016 |access-date=8 January 2019 |archive-date=3 December 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211203110555/https://www.uschina.org/media/press/uscbc-announces-relaunch-china-business-review |url-status=live }}</ref>

== Activities ==
The USCBC has consistently lobbied against designating China a [[currency manipulator]].<ref>{{Cite book |last=Hung |first=Ho-fung |title=Clash of Empires: From 'Chimerica' to the 'New Cold War' |date=2022-04-30 |publisher=[[Cambridge University Press]] |isbn=978-1-108-89589-7 |edition=1 |pages=41 |doi=10.1017/9781108895897}}</ref>

A 2021 study commissioned by the USCBC stated that the [[First Trump tariffs|Trump tariffs]] on Chinese goods directly resulted in the loss of 245,000 American jobs.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Kleiman |first=Michael |date=2021-01-01 |title=The US-China Economic Relationship: A Crucial Partnership At A Critical Juncture |url=https://www.oxfordeconomics.com/resource/the-us-china-economic-relationship-a-crucial-partnership-at-a-critical-juncture/ |access-date=2024-11-03 |website=Oxford Economics |language=en-US}}</ref><ref name=":Ma&Kang">{{Cite book |last=Ma |first=Xinru |title=Beyond Power Transitions: The Lessons of East Asian History and the Future of U.S.-China Relations |last2=Kang |first2=David C. |date=2024 |publisher=[[Columbia University Press]] |isbn=978-0-231-55597-5 |series=Columbia Studies in International Order and Politics |location=New York}}</ref>{{Rp|page=180}}

A 2021 report by the [[Foundation for Defense of Democracies]] identified USCBC as a key facilitator of Beijing's efforts to carry out its campaign of subnational influence in and against the United States.<ref>{{cite news |title=All Over the Map The Chinese Communist Party's Subnational Interests in the United States |url=https://www.politico.com/f/?id=0000017d-264b-df97-a9ff-be7f603e0000 |agency=Politico |publisher=FDD |pages=8–11 |access-date=2022-11-09 |archive-date=2021-11-18 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211118182412/https://www.politico.com/f/?id=0000017d-264b-df97-a9ff-be7f603e0000 |url-status=live }}</ref>

In 2022, the USCBC lobbied against legislation to screen of outbound U.S. investments for potential national security issues.<ref>{{Cite news |last1=O’Keeffe |first1=Kate |last2=Andrews |first2=Natalie |last3=Somerville |first3=Heather |date=2022-06-13 |title=Lawmakers Make Bipartisan Push for New Government Powers to Block U.S. Investments in China |language=en-US |work=[[The Wall Street Journal]] |url=https://www.wsj.com/articles/bipartisan-lawmakers-propose-new-government-powers-to-block-u-s-investments-in-china-other-nations-11655147194 |access-date=2022-06-14 |issn=0099-9660 |archive-date=2022-06-13 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220613235118/https://www.wsj.com/articles/bipartisan-lawmakers-propose-new-government-powers-to-block-u-s-investments-in-china-other-nations-11655147194 |url-status=live }}</ref> The council has also expressed concern about the implementation of the [[Uyghur Forced Labor Prevention Act]].<ref>{{Cite news |last=Garver |first=Rob |date=June 2, 2022 |title=US Prepares to Block Most Imports Tied to China's Xinjiang Province |url=https://www.voanews.com/a/us-prepares-to-block-most-imports-tied-to-china-s-xinjiang-province-/6601017.html |access-date=2022-06-18 |website=[[Voice of America]] |language=en |archive-date=2022-06-09 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220609110328/https://www.voanews.com/a/us-prepares-to-block-most-imports-tied-to-china-s-xinjiang-province-/6601017.html |url-status=live }}</ref> The USCBC has lobbied against the expansion of U.S. [[Export control|export controls]], especially the expansion of the [[Entity List]].<ref>{{Cite news |last=Swanson |first=Ana |date=2025-10-30 |title=In China Truce on Tariffs and Rare Earths, National Security Controls Are Bargaining Chip |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2025/10/30/us/politics/china-trump-trade-security-chips-minerals.html |access-date=2025-10-31 |work=[[The New York Times]] |language=en}}</ref>

In 2023, the USCBC and the [[National Committee on United States–China Relations]] hosted a banquet with [[General Secretary of the Chinese Communist Party]] [[Xi Jinping]] for US business executives during the [[APEC United States 2023]] meeting.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Martina |first=Michael |date=2023-11-14 |title=Tricky politics on menu for China's Xi at US business dinner |language=en |work=[[Reuters]] |url=https://www.reuters.com/world/tricky-politics-menu-chinas-xi-us-business-dinner-2023-11-14/ |access-date=2023-11-15 |archive-date=2023-11-14 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231114162632/https://www.reuters.com/world/tricky-politics-menu-chinas-xi-us-business-dinner-2023-11-14/ |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Swanson |first=Ana |date=2023-11-08 |title=Xi Jinping to Address U.S. Business Leaders Amid Rising Skepticism of China Ties |language=en-US |work=[[The New York Times]] |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2023/11/08/business/economy/xi-jinping-american-business-leaders-dinner.html |access-date=2023-11-15 |issn=0362-4331 |archive-date=2023-11-13 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231113192559/https://www.nytimes.com/2023/11/08/business/economy/xi-jinping-american-business-leaders-dinner.html |url-status=live }}</ref> The banquet drew |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231115034058/https://www.nysun.com/article/the-high-cost-40000-for-a-filet-mignon-of-dining-with-xi-jinping |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Jacob |first=Gu |date=November 14, 2023 |title=Xi's Arrival in US Brings Protesters and Fans Onto Streets |work=[[Bloomberg News]] |url=https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2023-11-14/china-s-xi-begins-first-us-trip-in-six-years-amid-tight-security |access-date=November 14, 2023 |quote=The Republican wrote to the US-China Business Council and National Committee on US-China Relations demanding the organizers provide details of the guest list, funding and profits. Neither group responded to Bloomberg’s request for comment on the dinner. |archive-date=November 14, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231114231158/https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2023-11-14/china-s-xi-begins-first-us-trip-in-six-years-amid-tight-security |url-status=live }}</ref> Some commentators and scholars have called for the [[Internal Revenue Service]] (IRS) to investigate USCBC's tax-exempt status for potential violations of "political and legislative lobbying."<ref>{{Cite book |last=Shambaugh |first=David |author-link=David Shambaugh |title=Breaking the Engagement: How China Won & Lost America |date=2025-08-21 |publisher=[[Oxford University Press]] |isbn=978-0-19-779242-1 |edition=1 |pages=285 |language=en |doi=10.1093/oso/9780197792421.001.0001 |oclc=1503438055}}</ref>
